 News › News News › Schools closed tomorrow in Andhra Pradesh and Chennai due to Cyclone Murasu: Check latest school hol… Schools closed tomorrow in Andhra Pradesh and Chennai due to Cyclone Murasu: Check latest school holiday updates and affected areas
 Adhya Sarna Updated: Nov 2, 2026, 22:53 IST School Holiday due to Cyclone Murasu Monday, November 2, 2026 : District administrations in Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu have suspended classes and closed schools as Cyclone Murasu approaches the south Andhra Pradesh coast. 
 The closures are precautionary measures to protect students and staff. Another school holiday may be declared for November 3, 2026. 
 According to the India Meteorological Department ( IMD ) , Murasu is expected to intensify into a Severe Cyclonic Storm and cross the south Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Narsapur, close to Ongole, with winds of 100 to 110 kmph, gusting to 120 kmph, between 11.30PM on November 2 and 4.00AM on November 3. A red alert has been issued for Krishna, Guntur, Bapatla, Prakasam and Nellore districts, where extremely heavy rainfall is possible.
 School holiday in Chennai and Tiruvallur 
 The Chennai and Tiruvallur district administrations have declared a holiday for all schools and colleges on Monday, November 2, as a precautionary measure. The Regional Meteorological Centre has issued an orange alert for both districts, warning of heavy to very heavy rainfall. District Collector S. Malathi Helan announced the holiday for Chennai. North Tamil Nadu and Puducherry are expected to experience winds of 60 to 70 kmph, gusting to 80 kmph, from this evening into Tuesday morning.
 School holiday in Andhra Pradesh 
 Schools and colleges will remain closed in Andhra Pradesh's NTR District (Vijayawada), Palnadu, Nellore and Gudur. Authorities have said the institutions may be used as temporary cyclone shelters, while teaching and non-teaching staff remain on emergency duty for relief and restoration work. Regional media have reported that closures extend to four districts in total, and the list may change as the storm advances.
 The storm is also affecting other states as Odisha's Malkangiri district has closed schools and colleges from November 2 to 4.
 Guidance for Parents and Students 
 Closures have been announced district by district, and only the Chennai and Tiruvallur holidays are confirmed for November 2. No official decision for November 3, had been reported at the time of writing. Families should follow the official announcements of their District Collector. As one regional outlet noted, a holiday should be considered confirmed only once an official announcement is issued by the respective district Collectors.
 Residents of coastal districts are advised to:
 Avoid unnecessary travel, particularly near the coast and in waterlogged areas.
 Keep emergency contact numbers, drinking water and essential supplies ready.
 Stay away from the sea, and ensure fishermen do not venture out.
 Follow IMD bulletins and state disaster management advisories.
 Authorities have activated disaster response protocols, and further announcements on school reopening are expected once the storm has crossed the coast and conditions are assessed.
